questions.question_text: A person touches a hot pan and withdraws the hand before consciously identifying the pain. Which structure can coordinate this rapid reflex?
questions.explanation: A spinal reflex can be integrated in the spinal cord, allowing a rapid response before conscious processing is complete.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In a simple reflex arc, which neuron carries information from a receptor toward the central nervous system?
questions.explanation: A sensory or afferent neuron conducts impulses from a receptor toward the CNS; motor neurons carry commands away.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: At most chemical synapses, why does an impulse not normally pass directly as an electrical current from one neuron to the next?
questions.option_a: The synaptic cleft contains bone tissue
questions.option_b: The next neuron has no membrane
questions.option_c: The axon is disconnected from the cell body
questions.option_d: A neurotransmitter crosses the synaptic cleft and binds receptors on the next cell
questions.explanation: At chemical synapses, the presynaptic terminal releases neurotransmitter, which diffuses across the cleft and acts on postsynaptic receptors.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A demyelinating disorder damages myelin around peripheral axons. Which effect is most likely?
questions.option_c: Faster hormone synthesis by the thyroid
questions.explanation: Myelin electrically insulates axons and supports rapid saltatory conduction; damage can slow or block nerve impulses.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: During an acute fright response, which coordinated change is most consistent with increased sympathetic activity?
questions.option_b: Heart rate falls and intestinal motility rises
questions.option_c: The bladder empties immediately in every case
questions.option_d: Heart rate rises and digestive activity is reduced
questions.explanation: Sympathetic activity prepares the body for rapid action, commonly increasing heart rate and reducing gastrointestinal activity.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: After a meal, parasympathetic activity is prominent. Which response is most likely?
questions.option_a: Rapid pupil dilation and reduced salivation
questions.option_b: Increased digestive secretion and gut motility
questions.explanation: Parasympathetic activity supports “rest-and-digest” functions, including salivation, digestive secretion and gut motility.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A fluid-filled space around the brain and spinal cord helps cushion the CNS from mechanical shock. What is the fluid called?
questions.explanation: Cerebrospinal fluid circulates around and within the CNS and provides buoyancy and mechanical cushioning.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A lesion disrupts the brain’s regulation of thirst, body temperature and links to endocrine control. Which region is most likely affected?
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus helps regulate homeostasis, including temperature and thirst, and links neural control with endocrine pathways.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Most sensory information headed to the cerebral cortex is relayed through which structure, with olfaction being a notable exception?
questions.explanation: The thalamus relays most sensory information to the cerebral cortex; olfactory pathways are a classic exception.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A lesion disconnects the two cerebral hemispheres and impairs transfer of information between them. Which structure is most directly involved?
questions.explanation: The corpus callosum is a large bundle of commissural fibres connecting the left and right cerebral hemispheres.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Degeneration of dopamine-producing neurons in the substantia nigra is associated with which disorder?
questions.explanation: Parkinson disease is associated with loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra and impaired motor control.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: At the neuromuscular junction, which chemical messenger is released by a motor neuron to stimulate skeletal muscle?
questions.explanation: Motor neurons release acetylcholine at the neuromuscular junction; it binds muscle receptors and initiates a muscle action potential.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A spinal nerve’s dorsal root is selectively damaged while its ventral root remains intact. Which deficit is most expected in the corresponding region?
questions.option_a: Loss of all motor output only
questions.option_b: Loss of hormone secretion from the thyroid
questions.option_c: Loss or reduction of sensory input
questions.explanation: The dorsal root carries sensory afferent fibres into the spinal cord; the ventral root carries motor efferents out.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: In a typical spinal-cord cross-section, which arrangement is correct?
questions.option_a: Grey matter is central and white matter surrounds it
questions.option_b: White matter is central and grey matter surrounds it
questions.option_c: Grey matter lies only in the vertebral bones
questions.option_d: Both types are confined to the outer meninges
questions.explanation: In the spinal cord, grey matter forms a central butterfly-shaped region surrounded by white matter, unlike the broad arrangement in much of the cerebrum.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A patient can speak fluently but has difficulty understanding spoken language after a focal brain injury. Which cortical region is most likely affected?
questions.option_d: Primary motor cortex of the leg
questions.explanation: Wernicke area is associated with language comprehension; damage can impair understanding while speech may remain fluent but nonsensical.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A patient understands instructions but struggles to produce fluent speech after a focal cortical injury. Which region is classically implicated?
questions.explanation: Broca area is involved in speech production; damage commonly causes effortful, non-fluent speech with relatively better comprehension.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: After bilateral injury to a medial temporal structure, a person can recall childhood events but cannot reliably form new long-term episodic memories. Which structure is most likely damaged?
questions.explanation: The hippocampal formation is important for forming new declarative and episodic memories; older memories may be relatively preserved.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Stimulation of the left primary motor cortex produces movement mainly on the right side of the body. Which pathway crossing best explains this pattern for most corticospinal fibres?
questions.option_d: Crossing in the lumbar sympathetic chain
questions.explanation: Most corticospinal fibres cross at the pyramidal decussation in the caudal medulla, producing predominantly contralateral motor control.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A lesion in the temporal lobe is most likely to affect which function among these options?
questions.option_d: Primary control of voluntary leg movement
questions.explanation: Auditory cortex lies in the temporal lobe; other options are associated with different structures or systems.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A spinal-cord injury interrupts ascending sensory pathways below the lesion but spares descending motor pathways. Which outcome is most consistent?
questions.option_a: Increased visual acuity below the lesion
questions.option_b: Immediate loss of hormone production by all glands
questions.option_c: Reduced sensation below the lesion with some voluntary movement preserved
questions.option_d: Complete loss of sensation only above the lesion
questions.explanation: Ascending tracts carry sensory information toward the brain; if descending motor tracts are spared, some voluntary movement may remain.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A voluntary command is sent to skeletal muscles while an involuntary signal regulates gut smooth muscle. Which pairing identifies the motor divisions involved?
questions.option_a: The autonomic system exists only in the spinal cord
questions.option_b: Both systems carry only sensory impulses
questions.option_c: Somatic output controls glands only; autonomic output controls voluntary skeletal movement
questions.option_d: Somatic output mainly controls skeletal muscle; autonomic output regulates smooth muscle, cardiac muscle and glands
questions.explanation: The somatic motor division supplies skeletal muscle, whereas autonomic pathways regulate involuntary effectors including smooth and cardiac muscle and glands.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual verification: NCERT Biology textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
